skill.displayName: 框架核心工程师 命令与代码生成

llm.summary: This is a Weline-specific engineering guidance skill with disclosed repo-scoped code generation and command-registration behavior, not hidden or malicious activity.

dimensions.detail: The skill may lead the agent to edit project code and run `php bin/w command:upgrade` when command registration changes, which is purpose-aligned but should be expected by users installing it.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The inspected artifact is a single Markdown skill file with no executable scripts, dependencies, remote payload retrieval, install hooks, or nonempty install metadata.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill references Weline project documents, shared team conventions, an agent roster, and Chinese role identifiers; this is disclosed and coherent for a Weline/internal workflow but less portable outside that context.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No persistence mechanisms, background workers, credential access, memory writes, tool wrapping, or privilege escalation instructions were found.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The stated purpose and instructions align around CLI command creation, scaffolding, generated-code quality, PHP 8.4 compatibility, and Windows command quoting.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install this only for Weline framework work where the referenced project documents and team roles make sense. Expect it to guide code edits, command scaffolding, validation, and command metadata refreshes inside the repo; no hidden network, credential, or persistence behavior was found.
llm.findings:
[AS3] expected: The artifact lists repo-local Weline source documents under `dev/ai/skills/...`; it does not instruct enumeration of arbitrary installed skills or access to hidden peer-skill secrets.
[SQP-3] expected: The Chinese shared-standard and `@Weline-技术主管` references are organization-specific collaboration routing, not a security bypass; users outside that organization may find them irrelevant.
[EA3] expected: The cited collaboration section narrows ownership boundaries and asks escalation on blockers or cross-agent issues, which supports controlled scope rather than expanding it.
